ideas.working_title: One Text, Two Tokenizers: GPT-2 and GPT-4
ideas.story_question: How do the GPT-2 and GPT-4 tokenizers segment the same fixed multilingual sample, and which encoding choices explain any count differences?
ideas.case: Compare the gpt2 and cl100k_base encodings assigned to GPT-2 and GPT-4 in a pinned tiktoken source revision, using the same declared English, Hindi and Japanese strings for both.
ideas.place_period_version: OpenAI tiktoken repository commit 4e71bbe0c078468e00fefbf94b39849389f346e5, inspected 2026-10-24; historical code mapping, not a claim about current hosted model availability or billing.
ideas.intended_audience: General adult viewers who want to understand why words and tokens are different units.
ideas.purpose: Show a reproducible difference in segmentation, then explain the vocabulary, pre-tokenization and byte-level boundaries without claiming access to a proprietary model's internal behavior.
evidence_gaps: Choose the exact on-screen examples and check each scripted factual sentence against the pre-production claim worksheet in Phase 1.
If the script discusses pricing or current hosted models, obtain separate dated primary documentation before making those claims.
blocking_gaps: No Phase 1 project claim ledger or scripted-claim review has been completed. The saved measurements verify only fixed strings and a pinned package version.
ideas.readiness_note: Pinned official code checked. Token counts, byte spans and round trips were measured with tiktoken 0.14.0; a controlled pattern/rank comparison and a pre-production claim worksheet are saved under topics/001_ai_technology_explainers/RESEARCH_NOTES/. Phase 1 scripted-claim review remains open. Keep researching status; no episode created.
